classification.difficultyReason: Identify the number available and the number of ordered positions in three direct contexts, expressing each answer in permutation notation.

content.prompt: Answer the following using the notation ${}^{n}P_{r}$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: From a group of 10, three people line up to buy tickets. How many ways can this happen?

answer.worked: Three people are selected from 10 and their order in the line matters, so the number of ways is ${}^{10}P_{3}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Five cards are each labelled uniquely with one of the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Three of the five cards are placed down in a row. How many ways can the cards be arranged?

answer.worked: Three distinct cards are selected from five and their order in the row matters, so the number of arrangements is ${}^{5}P_{3}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: One hundred people each buy one ticket in a lottery. How many ways can the first three places be awarded?

answer.worked: Three different ticket holders are selected from 100 for the ordered first, second and third places, so the number of ways is ${}^{100}P_{3}$.
